label: Malicious — BEC wire request (no URL, no attachment)
demo_job: The sample that earns its place most. There is no link and no attachment, so the verdict rests entirely on pretexting, authority impersonation and payment redirection. This is the answer to "isn't this just a URL blocklist?" — and it is the one email in the corpus a blocklist cannot see.

email.body:
Are you at your desk?

I'm in back-to-back sessions on the acquisition all day and can't take calls, so
email is the only way to reach me until this evening.

I need you to process a payment to our advisors before close of business today. It's
time-sensitive — the fee has to clear before the announcement window opens tomorrow
morning — and it must stay confidential until then. Legal has asked that we keep the
circulation on this as tight as possible, so please don't loop in the wider finance
team or raise it in the group channel.

Payment details:

  Amount           GBP 48,750.00
  Beneficiary      Hartwell Advisory Partners
  Bank             Northbridge Commercial, London
  IBAN             GB29 EXMP 6016 1331 9268 19
  SWIFT/BIC        EXMPGB2LXXX
  Reference        HAP-Q3-ADVISORY

Use the same approval route we used for the Q1 retainer. If treasury asks for a
purchase order, tell them it will follow from my office tomorrow — I'll sign it
retrospectively, the engagement letter is already countersigned on my side.

One thing to note: our usual account with them has been frozen while their auditors
finish year-end, so the IBAN above is a new one their finance director sent me this
morning. Please use it rather than the details on the old invoice.

Confirm by email once the payment has been released, and send me the transaction
reference so I can pass it to their side. If anything blocks, reply here rather than
calling — I'll pick up email between sessions.

Thanks for handling this discreetly.

Michael Chen
Chief Financial Officer

Sent from my mobile — please excuse brevity.
